laHacienda.title: The Estate
laHacienda.subtitle: A story that began over a century ago
laHacienda.content_1: Around 1872, an eighteen-year-old young man named Antonio Bruzzoni left Cogoleto, Liguria, Italy, and embarked on a journey to Venezuela. Over the years, he built his life, his family, and an agricultural legacy dedicated to coffee.
laHacienda.content_2: Together with Tomasa Silva Silva, he formed a family whose descendants remain connected to these lands. The story of Hacienda Bruzzoni is not just the story of a property. It is the story of a family.
laHacienda.content_3: It is the memory of those who worked these mountains before us. And it is also a responsibility: deciding what we do today with what we received.
laHacienda.sanJose_desc: With about 30 hectares historically dedicated to coffee cultivation.
laHacienda.laSiberia_desc: With about 60 hectares historically linked to coffee cultivation.

nuestraHistoria.title: From Liguria to the mountains of Venezuela
nuestraHistoria.subtitle: A story worth continuing
nuestraHistoria.content_1: Antonio Bruzzoni was born around 1854 in Cogoleto, Liguria, Italy. At eighteen, he embarked on a journey to Venezuela, leaving behind his homeland to build a new life.
nuestraHistoria.content_2: Family memory tells that he may have traveled accompanied by a brother known as 'Yumin', although this episode is still part of the family's documentary research.
nuestraHistoria.content_3: In Venezuela, Antonio began to progressively build his legacy. The lands were incorporated through different mechanisms over time, including grants and acquisitions, until they formed the patrimonial ensemble we now know as Hacienda Bruzzoni.
nuestraHistoria.content_4: Coffee became the center of that activity. Generations later, its coffee plantations, infrastructure, and landscape remain as testimony to that effort.
nuestraHistoria.quote: The goal is not to turn the past into a museum piece. It is to make that past produce a future again.

biografia.title: Biography
biografia.content_1: Antonio Bruzzoni Delfino was born around 1854 in Cogoleto, Liguria, Italy. He was the son of Lázaro Bruzzoni and Benedetta Delfino.
biografia.content_2: At the end of the 19th century, at barely eighteen years old, he embarked on a journey to Venezuela, leaving his homeland to start a new life. According to family tradition, he may have traveled accompanied by a brother known as "Yumin", whose later history remains pending investigation within the family story.
biografia.content_3: In Venezuela, Antonio found a land to settle in. With effort, discipline and a capacity for risk-taking, he developed an agricultural estate in the mountains of Aragua, a region where coffee cultivation had deep historical roots.

familia.title: Family
familia.subtitle: Together with Tomasa Silva Silva
familia.content_1: Antonio shared his life with Tomasa Silva Silva, a Venezuelan woman, daughter of Juan Silva and Andrea Silva. Together they formed a family marked by effort, perseverance and also the difficulties of their time.
familia.content_2: Seven of their children reached adulthood and allowed the continuity of the family name and history:
familia.hijos: María Magdalena, Carmen, Modesta, Eugenio, Carlina Antonia, Teodora María and Luis.

legado.title: A legacy that transcends
legado.subtitle: More than an estate, a way of life
legado.content_1: Family memory describes Antonio as a hardworking, loving man dedicated to his children. Among the memories passed down, the image of Antonio reading while his children sat around him to listen stands out.
legado.content_2: Because building a legacy is not just about building properties. It is also about transmitting values.
legado.cita: "A legacy is not preserved just by remembering it. A legacy is preserved by taking action."

sanJose.title: San José (Bucaral)
sanJose.subtitle: Coffee land
sanJose.content_1: San José, also known as Bucaral, is part of the historical heritage of Hacienda Bruzzoni. With approximately 50 hectares, about 30 were historically linked to coffee cultivation.
sanJose.content_2: The recovery of these lands is part of the hacienda's productive vision. The project contemplates progressively evaluating the state of the coffee plantations, recovering viable areas, and rebuilding a productive chain capable of generating value from the farm itself.
sanJose.content_3: It is not just about planting again. It is about recovering knowledge, quality, identity, and purpose.

laSiberia.title: La Siberia
laSiberia.subtitle: A name born from the landscape
laSiberia.content_1: La Siberia comprises approximately 90 hectares of the family heritage. Its name, according to family tradition, was chosen by Antonio as a reference to the climatic characteristics of the place, which reminded him of the Russian region of Siberia.
laSiberia.content_2: Approximately 60 hectares are historically linked to coffee cultivation. La Siberia represents a fundamental part of the productive and natural potential of Hacienda Bruzzoni.
laSiberia.content_3: Its mountains, climate, vegetation, and landscapes also open possibilities for the development of nature, contemplation, and adventure experiences.

nuestroCafe.title: Coffee as heritage
nuestroCafe.subtitle: From the mountain to the cup
nuestroCafe.content_1: Coffee was the productive origin of this heritage. Today we want to recover that tradition and transform it into a contemporary quality proposal.
nuestroCafe.content_2: A brand born from a real story. A coffee whose origin is in the same lands that for generations have been linked to our family.
nuestroCafe.donAntonio_desc: The first expression of Bruzzoni Café will bear the name of the one who started this story. A tribute to a man who arrived in Venezuela very young and dedicated his life to building a family and a legacy in these mountains.
nuestroCafe.process_note: Productive recovery will be accompanied by technical evaluation and the search for specialized allies.

turismo.title: Live the mountain
turismo.subtitle: Nature, history and experiences
turismo.content: Hacienda Bruzzoni has the potential to become a place where nature, history and experiences meet. We don't just want to offer a place to visit. We want to create reasons to return.

elProyecto.title: A legacy for the future
elProyecto.subtitle: Family + Company + Heritage
elProyecto.content_1: Hacienda Bruzzoni is born from a family story. But its future requires a business vision. The purpose of the project is to create a structure capable of preserving the heritage, developing productive activities, generating income, and progressively increasing the value of the estate.
elProyecto.content_2: The vision contemplates the creation of a family business, whose legal structure, participation and rights must be defined with professional advice and through the corresponding agreements among family members.
elProyecto.pillar_1_desc: A project that unites different generations
elProyecto.pillar_2_desc: An organized structure to manage the heritage
elProyecto.pillar_3_desc: Preserve, develop and transmit the legacy
elProyecto.quote: Not everyone has to do the same thing. The project must allow different forms of participation.

naturaleza.title: Produce without losing what makes this place special
naturaleza.subtitle: A balance between production, conservation and responsible use
naturaleza.content_1: Nature is not a decorative element of Hacienda Bruzzoni. It is one of its main assets. Therefore, future development must seek a balance between production, conservation and responsible use of the territory.
naturaleza.content_2: Possibilities may include sustainable agriculture, coffee recovery, beekeeping, nature experiences and other activities that are technically and environmentally viable.
naturaleza.principle: Create value without destroying the natural heritage that generates that value.
